title: Neue Grafik journal
lede: The trilingual Zürich journal that stated the style’s principles and printed them as a four-column grid on every cover.
summary: Neue Grafik / New Graphic Design / Graphisme actuel, 18 issues, 1958–1965.

source.label: eMuseum, Museum für Gestaltung Zürich: Neue Grafik no. 1

creator.name: Richard Paul Lohse, Josef Müller-Brockmann, Hans Neuburg, and Carlo Vivarelli (editors); cover design Carlo Vivarelli

evidence.note: Downloaded the cover scan of issue 16, July 1963 ([File:Neue Grafik July 1963.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Neue_Grafik_July_1963.jpg), 2953 × 3307 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. Issue 1 data and description read on eMuseum records 23096 and 44032. The image is not stored.

styles.note: The style’s own manifesto and showcase; Wikipedia says it disseminated the style’s tenets and was key to its emergence as a movement.

context: Neue Grafik was a quarterly founded in Zürich on 15 February 1958 by Josef Müller-Brockmann, Hans Neuburg, Richard Paul Lohse, and Carlo Vivarelli. Eighteen issues appeared from 1958 to 1965. [Wikipedia: Neue Grafik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Grafik).

Issue 1, September 1958: letterpress, 28 × 24.8 cm, 75 pages, published and printed by Verlag Otto Walter AG, Olten; cover design Carlo Vivarelli. [eMuseum object 23096](https://www.emuseum.ch/objects/23096), [cover, object 44032](https://www.emuseum.ch/objects/44032).

The eMuseum description of issue 1 notes Akzidenz Grotesk for the headings and Monotype 215 for the texts, and a cover of four columns in which only the issue number changes. [eMuseum object 44032](https://www.emuseum.ch/objects/44032).

Wikipedia notes the journal’s advocacy of photography as a central element of graphic design, and criticism in Zürich that the style was rigid and cold. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Grafik).
observed: Issue 16 cover: the three-language title stacks in three lines of large black grotesque at top left, tightly spaced.
Below the title, the page divides into four columns: contributors’ names in the first, then German, English, and French contents in parallel.
The issue number “16” is the only other large element, set in the first column at the same size as the title.
Everything is black on white and flush left; there are no rules, images, or color.
Large empty bands separate the title, the subtitle row, and the contents.
interpretation: The cover is a table of contents made into a composition. It demonstrates the style’s claim that correct organization of information is itself the design.
The fixed template, with only the number changing, treats the journal as a system rather than a series of individual covers.
borrow: Use parallel columns for parallel languages or versions, aligned line for line.
Design a fixed cover or page template where a single variable, such as a number or date, carries the change.
Let the table of contents be the hero of an index page.
related: Published by the editors of [Der Film](ref:der-film-poster-1960) and set in [Akzidenz-Grotesk](ref:akzidenz-grotesk-typeface).
